blocking.section: Recommended exact spec diff: partition ordering and no-token defaults; §§10.1/11/12.3

steps.claim: Only oracle_call has a separate tk operand. action_call has mutable, input, memory and classical-argument lists, with no primary token.

The proposal instead prepends a separate token for region requests, says every region without token arguments has [0], and requires executors to derive partitions from actual live handles. Its no-separate-token exception names only CC/R entries.

The published controlled-action fixture calls flip with no token operands. Its actual token list is empty, but the proposal's region default requires [0]. For an action with one token argument a, the same omission leaves no source rule deciding whether a hypothetical primary token aliases a, distinguishing [0,0] from [0,1].

Consequently, action invocation partitions cannot be derived consistently between source execution, estimation and certificate replay. The premise that every region invocation supplies a primary token is false; this affects mandatory binding arity and schedule matching.

blocking.fix: In §§10.1/11/12.3 and both no-token defaults, state: “For an oracle invocation, list its separate invocation token first, followed by token-typed arguments in signature order. For an action, permutation action or CC/R entry, list only token-typed parameters in signature order. Budget fields do not create token identities. The separate budget token accepted by the estimation ABI contributes an identity slot only when the subject is an oracle.” Correct examples: a token-free oracle has [0]; token-free controlled and flip actions have []; an action receiving a,b has [0,0] for one shared identity and [0,1] for distinct identities. Alternatively, define an explicit action context-token mechanism and its runtime propagation, but I recommend omitting the nonexistent primary identity because this preserves §4.7 and source hashes.

blocking.section: Release and route; mixed-fat-object standing check
blocking.problem: The proposal changes launch support, invocation identity and certificate bindings, but neither it nor INDEX's publication section states how a native-host-plus-marked-device-modules fat object uses them. The general assertion that no North Star capability is removed does not supply the explicit mixed-object application required by the standing check.
blocking.fix: Add to Release and route: “A mixed fat object retains its native host binary and carries ISA objects and device certificates for marked device modules and their linked device closure. These token partitions are scoped to invocations of a loaded device program, not to the whole native binary. The launch runtime derives entry partitions from valid device token handles and preserves equality through device calls; serialization records equality classes only. Native host-only functions need no device certificate, and this repair does not require moving host entry points, argv/envp or the native libc closure into an ISA object.”

suggestions: ABI compatibility paragraph: adopt the explicit default “A legacy request with token arguments and no partition returns E_ARG; the new entry point supports every consistent partition.” If retaining uniform legacy results, state instead: “A K12 result returned through the legacy ABI must be exact for every consistent partition and carry an explicitly universal binding; a worst-case bound must use a separately identified result kind.” I recommend the first route for this repair.

Hashes, catalog and consumers: add “Changing launch/sched/cert versions in an object header changes object_hash even when symbol envelopes remain unchanged; regenerate object bindings and downstream certificate pins. Under an authorized feature-only repair with unchanged header/source bytes, object and symbol hashes remain unchanged, while modified schedule hashes and certificate bytes must be regenerated.” The independently recomputed ref catalog envelope remains 5de4e4995350313e50217880ba1b95de39cd043283b726337d4894efb005d197.

Inverse-pair conformance: add “An entry with primary budget (2,0,0,0), argument-token tuple (2,0,0,0) and partition [0,0] does not cover primary budget (3,0,0,0) with that unchanged argument tuple: [0,0] is tuple-inconsistent, while [0,1] changes the certified partition.” This makes the proposed preservation of equality constraints under budget coverage directly testable.
path_to_accept: 1. Define action partitions without an invented primary identity and update the ABI defaults and examples accordingly. 2. Add the explicit mixed-fat-object application paragraph. These are the two acceptance blockers; the remaining recommendations are discretionary.
summary: The identity defect is real and the canonical-partition repair is sound in principle. Revise the false generalization that every region has a primary token, and explicitly preserve mixed-fat-object use. Tuple hashes and catalog-preservation claims check out subject to the stated publication route.
